text:
maya: quick heads-up — after rolling calico 3.26.1 to us-west-2-prod this morning we started seeing intermittent pod-to-pod packet loss for GPU training jobs (RDMA-enabled). A few job shards failed with timeouts.

sam: saw it too, reproducing on a single node with two g4dn pods. latency spikes + packet drops on east-west traffic.

lee: more details? same-node or cross-node?

maya: mostly same-node, but cross-node also affected in some AZs. I ran a quick iperf3 between pods:

```
# iperf3 -c 10.0.20.12 -t 30
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  4]   0.00-30.00  sec  6.12 GBytes  1.76 Gbits/sec  (lossy)
```

maya: tcpdump shows a lot of retransmits and occasional ICMP "Fragmentation needed" msgs. Snippet: 

```
17:12:04.123456 IP pod-a > pod-b: Flags [P.], seq 1:1457, ack 1, win 229, length 1456
17:12:04.123457 IP pod-b > pod-a: ICMP 3 4 unreachable, mtu 1400
```

jon: ICMP fragmentation needed -> MTU mismatch on overlay. Calico should auto-detect MTU but 3.26 introduced change to default encapsulation lookup. Could be IPIP or VXLAN default switching.

anna: Confirming — our calico configmap has `tunnel: "ipip"` still, but I see Felix reporting `Detected MTU mismatch` in logs after upgrade.

sam: I dug into felix logs: `Detected route MTU 9000, interface mtu 1500, overlay mtu calc 1418` then later `Unable to fragment` errors. Probably jumbo frames + ENA offload + wrong GENEVE header assumptions.

lee: Are RDMA jobs using host devices / SR-IOV? If so, some offload interactions can break when encapsulation size changes.

maya: Yes, training pods request `rdma=true` via device plugin on those instances. Our qps drops align with pods that bind NICs for RDMA.

jon: Action plan: 1) rollback calico to 3.25.2 on the node pool with GPUs, 2) run controlled test, 3) collect tcpdump, `ip -s link`, Felix logs, and iperf.

anna: I'm starting the rollback on the gpu-nodepool DaemonSet now — patching image tag to `calico/node:v3.25.2`. Will cordon+drain one node at a time.

infra-bot: deploy-triggered: rollout started for daemonset calico-node in namespace kube-system by anna. rollout_id=roll-20250318-01

sam: while rollback runs, can we try a workaround: set `vethMTUOverride: 1400` in ConfigMap and `felix.ipipMTU=1400`? That may avoid fragmentation messages.

lee: good idea for canary. But changing MTU cluster-wide is risky — prefer nodepool-scoped change or annotation.

maya: I applied a patch on a single canary GPU node: edited calico-config to include `vethMTUOverride: "1410"` and restarted the pod. Can confirm iperf improved — sustained ~9 Gbps within node with low retransmits.

```
# ip -s link show tunl0
5: tunl0: <POINTOPOINT,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1410 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 12345 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 23456789 packets 23456 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 carrier 0 collisions 0
```

jon: ok that is consistent. So 3.26 changed MTU calc/encapsulation defaults for certain kernel/ENA combos causing overlay <-> host MTU mismatch, which breaks fragmentation for RDMA/ENABLED offloads.

anna: rollback progress: 4/8 gpu nodes rolled back, drains succeeded. Initial telemetry looks better on rolled nodes (jobs resumed).

sam: open a ticket with Calico upstream? We should include: kernel version, ENA driver version, calico config, Felix logs, debug tar, and tcpdumps. I'll start drafting.

lee: also postmortem items: 1) add calico upgrade canary to gpu nodepool before cluster-wide, 2) a smoke test including iperf3 + RDMA ping (ib_ping) for GPU nodes, 3) run `mtu probe` check as part of upgrade job.

maya: agreed. For immediate mitigation we have: rolled back to 3.25.2 on GPU pool, applied `vethMTUOverride: 1410` on one canary where rollback hasn't finished, and postponed rest of calico upgrades.

anna: FYI I've moved some long-running training jobs to us-east-1 where calico is still on 3.25 and capacity exists.

jon: thanks all. Sam/Lee/Maya — please collect debug bundle and open the calico issue. Tag me and infra lead. I'll coordinate with SRE to run a full cluster-wide MTU validation.

sam: started the calico upstream bug: https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/9876 (draft) — attaching felix logs and tcpdump.

maya: relaying customer impact: two internal experiments lost checkpoints and had to restart. Not a customer-facing outage but could affect SLAs for enterprise trials. Noted in incident tracker.

infra-bot: incident-created: INC-2025-0443 linked to thread 1791201234 by maya

lee: final note — when we reattempt upgrade, we'll run it against a small canary pool with RDMA+GPU to validate overlay behaviour. Also add `--set ipipMTU` explicitly in deploy chart to avoid calico guessing.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with postmortem draft once we gather artifacts. :thumbsup:
